title: Rust decode_rule255 must not apply endpoint address policy (spec 03 Rule255 canonical TX/RX split)
description: Child of project-LICHEN-worker6-k0r2; keystone spec work already landed (spec/03-adaptation.md 'Endpoint address policy (canonical TX/RX split)': emission policy applies to every transmitted packet incl. Rule255 ENCODE; DECODING is byte-preserving, MUST validate structure+checksums only, MUST NOT apply the endpoint address policy, so 'a packet one implementation cannot originate is still delivered intact by the other'). Python verified aligned: headers.py encode_rule255:188-189 and compression fallback :860-861 run _validate_rule255_emission_endpoints; decode_rule255:212 runs structural validation only. Rust violates the RX half: rust/lichen-schc/src/codec.rs decode_rule255 (:1444 area) routes through validate_full_ipv6 (:279) -> validate_address_policy (:241-263) and returns Err(InvalidPacket) on loopback/IPv4-mapped/bad-scope endpoints (k0r2 trigger bytes: src ::1, src ::ffff:192.0.2.1, dst ::1, dst ff01::1 scope 1, dst ff0f::1 scope 15) - identical on-air bytes decode in Python and fatal in Rust, and inflate RuleVersionFailureTracker via decompress_authenticated_frame_tracked (:1470-1482). Fix: decode_rule255 (and any RX-side full-packet validation reachable from it) must validate version/length/next-header/UDP length/checksum structure but NOT the endpoint policy; keep the TX paths (compress gate :2140, encode_rule255 :1414) enforcing validate_address_policy. Prefer an explicit split (e.g. structural validator used by decode vs TX validator) over a bool flag if it reads cleaner; keep public API churn minimal and document the RX/TX split in the doc comments. Pin with unit tests: decode_rule255 ACCEPTS the five k0r2 trigger classes; encode_rule255 still REJECTS them.
close_reason: Both halves of the k0r2 divergence were already implemented at HEAD (spec canonical TX/RX split landed in faed8ccfb5; Rust codec.rs already split validate_full_ipv6_structure (RX, policy-free) from validate_full_ipv6 (TX, structure+policy); Python already enforces _validate_rule255_emission_endpoints on encode+fallback and decodes emission-free). What was actually broken: (a) Python validate_rule7_addresses still raised stale 'invalid Rule 7 ...' texts from 95d85c3747 while the shared-vector test (faed8ccfb5) pins canonical 'invalid IPv6 ...' texts matching Rust - 10 rule7_*_rejected vectors failed fleet-wide on main; fixed the 3 message texts; python/tests/test_vectors.py 767/767. (b) Rust codec.rs endpoint-policy tests never compiled (Ipv6Addr::from_str without FromStr in scope); added use core::str::FromStr as _; in tests mod; cargo test -p lichen-schc --features std green (81 lib + all suites, incl. rule255_emission_rejects_policy_invalid_endpoints and rule255_decode_is_byte_preserving_despite_emission_policy); no_std lib build verified clean. 3x codereview (correctness/security/robustness, reviewer-model passes): all PASS, no new P0-P3 (one P3 env note duplicates the already-filed rust-oscore/Attic-paths blocker). Remaining k0r2 work tracked by child 1jbb (shared Rule255 endpoint-policy vectors consistency check + parity script rerun + close parent).
